content: Before using this medication, carefully read and follow all instructions provided on the product packaging. If you have any questions, consult your pharmacist for clarification. Apply ivermectin lotion only to dry hair and scalp. Use enough lotion, up to one full tube, to thoroughly coat and cover all of your hair from the roots to the ends, as well as your entire scalp. Leave the lotion on for a full 10 minutes, then rinse it off with water. For children, an adult should apply the medication on their behalf. Do not use this medication on your eyebrows or eyelashes. Avoid contact with your eyes. If the lotion accidentally gets into your eyes, flush them immediately with water. Do not swallow this medication, and do not apply it to your mouth, nose, vagina, or any other areas of your body. This medication is intended for single use only. Discard any unused lotion after application. Common side effects may include eye redness or irritation, dry skin, or a stinging or burning sensation. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of potential side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this medication are rare. However, this is not a complete list of possible side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar guidance. Before using ivermectin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. The oral form of ivermectin is known to pass into breast milk in small amounts, but it is unclear if the topical form does the same. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, as well as herbal products, and share this list with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. To prevent the spread of lice, wash all recently used clothing, hats, bedding, and towels in hot water or have them dry-cleaned. Store this medication at room temperature and do not freeze it. This medication is for single use only, so discard any unused lotion. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly dispose of this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
